---
title: "Hide Inline Code"
filters:
  - regurgitate
extensions:
  regurgitate:
    show-code-inline: false
---

Sometimes you want a clean, narrative-focused document where readers see only results—not code. Setting `show-code-inline: false` removes code from its original positions while preserving all output. The complete source code moves to the appendix.

This approach works well for executive summaries, journal articles, or any document where the story matters more than the implementation.

```yaml
extensions:
  regurgitate:
    show-code-inline: false
```

## Quarterly Sales Analysis

Our analysis examines sales performance across four quarters:

```{python}
# Quarterly sales data (in thousands)
quarters = ["Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"]
sales = [142, 168, 155, 189]

total = sum(sales)
average = total / len(sales)
growth = (sales[-1] - sales[0]) / sales[0] * 100

print("=== Quarterly Sales Report ===")
print(f"Total Annual Sales: ${total}K")
print(f"Average per Quarter: ${average:.1f}K")
print(f"Q1 to Q4 Growth: {growth:.1f}%")
print(f"Best Quarter: {quarters[sales.index(max(sales))]} (${max(sales)}K)")
```

## Statistical Summary

```{r}
# Summary statistics for the built-in mtcars dataset
cat("=== Vehicle Performance Summary ===\n\n")
cat("Miles per Gallon:\n")
print(summary(mtcars$mpg))
cat("\nHorsepower:\n")
print(summary(mtcars$hp))
```

---

*Notice how the sections above show only the output—no code blocks interrupt the narrative. Readers who want to see the implementation can find everything in the appendix.*
